question_text: Was the RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer break-in a hack?
answer_text: Yes, by RIKEN's own account: an outside party got into Fugaku's operational network from Nov 10 to 13, installed malicious programs on some servers and took users' files, including private keys. Who did it is not known.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How did the attacker get into Fugaku?
answer_text: RIKEN says through the publicly reachable operating-status dashboard. The exact method is still under investigation.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were the stolen keys used to break into other computers?
answer_text: RIKEN says the intruder tried to connect to other systems with some of the stolen credentials. It has found no other misuse so far, and it has not confirmed any break-in elsewhere.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: RIKEN or another operator reporting a confirmed break-in using a stolen key, or RIKEN stating that none happened.

question_text: Was my Fugaku or RIKYU account information taken?
answer_text: RIKEN says names, emails, user IDs and registration details were or may have been taken for up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 RIKYU users, and it is contacting them. If you kept private keys on Fugaku, replace them everywhere.
label: Confirmed

what_would_settle_it: RIKEN, police or a credible researcher naming the attacker, or a verified claim of responsibility.

question_text: When will Fugaku be back online?
what_would_settle_it: RIKEN announcing a restart date after its security measures and server rebuild.
